story.name: トウキョウ ひとりぐらし
story.title: Three in the Morning
story.line: ブーケが よなかの コンビニに いきます
story.ja: 時差ぼけで夜中の3時に目がさめたブーケは、角のコンビニへ。夜勤の大学生レムに鮭の弁当を温めてもらい、袋もはしも「イエス」。おにぎりの開け方（1、2、3の順）を教わるが、2つ目でのりがやぶれてしまう。川べりで卵サンドを食べ、空が明るくなったころ、とつぜんの夏の大雨。ずぶぬれのブーケを、散歩帰りのアリゲッティが紺色の大きな傘に入れてくれ、「しばらく使って。返すのはいつでも」とそのまま貸してくれる。

segments.en: Rosie opened her eyes. The room was dark. For a moment, she had no idea where she was, or why the floor smelled like grass.
Then she remembered. Tokyo. The tatami. Her phone said it was three in the morning, and she was wide awake.
Oh no. This is jet lag, isn't it? My body thinks it's lunchtime. And I'm starving. I haven't eaten since the plane.
There was nothing in her kitchen but a bottle of water and some tea bags from her mom. So she put on her sneakers and went out.
The street was empty. But down at the corner there was a light, big and bright, like a lighthouse in the dark.
It was a convenience store, open all night, like they always are in Japan. The doors slid open with a little song.
Inside, it was cool and clean and full of everything. Rice balls. Sandwiches. Hot drinks in a warm little case. Ice cream. Socks. Even neckties.
Behind the counter was a sleepy young goat with a name tag that said Sherb, a college student working the night shift.
Oh, hey. Good morning. Or, um, good night? Honestly, I'm not sure anymore at this hour. Take your time.
Rosie took her time. She picked out an egg sandwich, two rice balls, a little box of salmon and rice, and, after some thought, a pudding.
Want me to heat that up for you? It only takes like a minute. And do you need a bag? Chopsticks?
Yes, please. And yes to the bag, and yes to chopsticks. And no, sorry, I don't have a points card. I just got here.
No worries. Hey, is this your first konbini rice ball? Here, let me show you. There's a trick to it.
He picked up one of the rice balls and showed her the little numbers printed on the plastic. One, two, three.
Pull number one, straight down the middle. Then two, then three. And that's it. The seaweed stays nice and crispy.
Rosie tried the second one herself. She pulled number one. Then number three. Then number two.
The seaweed tore in half and stayed stuck inside the plastic. The rice fell into her hand in one big lump.
Hey, that's okay. Everybody messes it up the first time. It still tastes the same. Seriously, don't worry about it.
Thank you. Really. You're only the third person I've really talked to in Tokyo. Thanks, Sherb.
She ate the egg sandwich on a bench by the river. It was soft and sweet and perfect.
Slowly, the sky turned gray, then pink. An old man walked by with a tiny dog in a stroller. A crow said something loud from a power line.
And then, with no warning at all, it started to rain. Not a gentle rain. A big summer rain, warm and heavy, all at once.
Oh, come on! Seriously? It was totally clear a second ago!
She ran home with the plastic bag over her head. By the time she reached her street, she was soaked. Only the pudding was dry.
At the corner, someone was standing under a big navy umbrella with a wooden handle. It was Gayle, coming home from her morning walk.
Good morning, dear! My goodness, look at you. Come here, come under. The weather changes its mind fast in summer.
They walked home together under the big umbrella. At the front door, Gayle closed it, shook it once, and handed it to Rosie.
Here. Keep this for now. It's supposed to rain all week, and you start work tomorrow, don't you? I have more umbrellas than I need.
Are you sure? Thank you so much. I'll bring it right back, I promise. As soon as the rain stops.
Oh, there's no hurry. Bring it back whenever. That's what neighbors are for.
Upstairs, Rosie leaned the umbrella by her door, where she would see it. Then she ate the pudding, very slowly, and watched the rain.
She fell asleep again right there by the window, with the spoon still in her hand. This time, she slept until noon.

ph.ja: すっかり目がさえている
ph.trap: wide＝広い ではなく「完全に」
時間を取る ではなく、急がなくていいよ

ph.scene: a boxed meal at the counter
ph.trap: up で「しっかり温める」。コンビニの「温めますか？」
mess＝散らかす。mess up でやりそこなう
おいで ではなく、不満やあきれた気持ち
for now＝ずっと ではなく「さしあたり」
隣人の目的 ではなく、気にしないでという決まり文句

predict.ask: ブーケは つぎに どこへ いく？
choices: Back to the convenience store, to apply for a job.
To Gayle's door, to give the umbrella back the next day.
To the ward office, to register her new address.
predict.ja: 区役所へ行き、新しい住所を届ける。
